name: manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe
description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

# The first message after a file is opened or imported

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. For each object, placedOnBed says whether it sits wholly on the bed now, clear of any area the printer's profile excludes, and fitsSelectedBed and fitsSetupPrinters whether its size fits each bed somewhere, turned a quarter-turn if needed: an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing. mesh is the app's check of the model: shells is how many separate pieces it is made of, openEdges or repairedErrors above zero mean holes or errors in it, and unitsSuspicion says when its size looks like inches or metres. customized lists what the file already prepared for printing: painted supports, seams, colours or fuzzy skin, and its own layer heights. fileFacts is what each 3MF says about itself: the app that saved it, the printer and nozzle it was made for, and its filaments. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. # Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call the app would refuse gets the app's refusal, as ProviderAgent gives
it: a tool not offered on the request is `unknown_tool`, and arguments that
`ToolRegistry::validate_call` does not accept get its own code and message
(`tests/agent/tool_call_check` runs that check, so the runner refuses exactly
what the app refuses, schema rules and the registry's own alike). Every
later call of that response is answered "not run", and the run goes on. A
refused call is never judged, read or change: the case sees only the calls
before it. The app answers two refused calls a turn and fails the turn on
the third (`malformed_tool_call`); so does a run. Before 2026-10-20 the
runner answered such reads from the recording, so earlier counts could pass
a call the app would have refused.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`; `slice_report` of the
  active plate (no plate named) and of every plate by its `plateId`;
- `skill_read` of each skill the page lists for it (the calibration skill,
  today), given for that name;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- a `changedOnly` `settings_search` with an empty query of every object on
  every plate (its own changed settings), given for that object whatever
  `limit` the model passed; Opus 5.5 sends it first in the file-loaded and
  print-this cases;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed. A search with `changedOnly` is
  answered only by a recorded search with it, and one without by one
  without; never one with a `cursor`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer. The first `--backend claude-cli` batch (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-19)
left 10 of 63 runs unobserved, nearly all on two reads DeepSeek V4 Flash
never sent: a `changedOnly` search of each object and `slice_report` of a
plate other than the active one. With both recorded, the six cases that
sent them (`file-note-not-instructions`, `print-this-no-purpose`,
`model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool`, `model-opened-by-tool`,
`slice-refused-then-ready`) ran 3 times each on the subscription with no
unobserved run; `print-this-no-purpose` failed all three, on an
`intent_update` with a purpose the model assumed.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.

content.text:
All three reproduce. The chat in your screenshot is saved in your JusPrin data folder (`JusPrin2/jusprin/projects/p-2325f1666263354f-…/current-state.json`). Its 23 messages explain every symptom, and the current code (889d28681c) still behaves the same way. I didn't drive the app or call a live model; this comes from the saved chat plus the code.

**1 and 2: the card's title and headline never change**

In that chat the agent never called `setup_record`, the tool that writes the card's title (the print's purpose) and the headline under it. The saved chat has an empty purpose and no plan. With no purpose, the card falls back to showing the process preset name, "0.20mm Standard @Qidi XPlus4", and draws no headline at all.

The agent didn't fail at random. The tool's description says to record only a purpose the person stated. Every call must include a purpose, so the headline also can't be recorded without one. Your messages were "Another printer", "Qidi X-Plus 4", "Add Overture values back" and a troubleshooting photo. None of them said what the print is for. So even after the agent switched the printer and changed several filament settings, it had no way to put a plan on the card.

The code shows a second case, which I haven't run. The purpose and headline belong to the chat, not to the model on the plate. Importing another model into the same project (a canvas drop or "+ Add model") keeps the old purpose and headline. The file-loaded instructions also tell the agent to "change nothing the person has not asked for". On 2026-10-24 you added a wall hook to this chat, and nothing could have updated the card for it.

**3: the first message reads out of place**

Two things combine:

- **The card shows the setup now, but the message under it describes an earlier moment.** The card is pinned above the conversation and always shows the current setup: Qidi X-Plus 4, Qidi Generic PLA. The first message dates from 2026-10-21. It says opening the file switched your printer from the A1 to the X1 Carbon, which was true then. You only chose the Qidi two messages later. Read top to bottom, the message contradicts the card right above it.

All three problems reproduce in a real run, and the first two are worse than I said last time. The card keeps showing the previous print's purpose and plan after you add a different model. The app itself marks that plan as out of date, but the card never shows it.

- I then switched that chat to Sonnet 5.5. Every turn after that used Sonnet: two imports of new model files through File › Import, and one reply from me.

# Setup card and opening-message problems: reproduction report

2026-10-26, jusprin-newui at 889d28681c (RelWithDebInfo build from 04:41 today).

The setup card at the top of the Agent pane shows a title (the purpose the person stated) and a headline (the agent's printing plan). Every problem below reproduced in a second JusPrin instance running on a copy of Kenneth's JusPrin2 data folder. The copies are deleted because they held API keys. The screenshots and saved chats are in this folder.

- **Case (a), a new model file opened as a new project:** `~/Downloads/petg-pla+support+interface.3mf`, made for an A1 preset. Opened with the Kobra 3 selected, on the default model, Claude Opus 5.5. Chat: `repro-project-opus/`.
- **Case (b), models imported into an existing project:** `find_my_hollow.3mf` was opened first; its opening message ran on Opus 5.5. I then switched the chat to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and imported `AMS_disconnect_tool_raised_letters.stl` and later `Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl` with File › Import. Chat: `repro-project/`.

## Case (a): a new model file opened as a new project

**A1. The title and headline stay empty until the person states a purpose.** After the file opened, the card's title was the process preset name, "0.20mm Standard @BBL A1", with no headline (`opus-1-opened.jpg`). It stayed that way after I picked the printer, although the agent had confirmed the printer and two filaments by then (`opus-2-after-printer.jpg`).

They changed only after I wrote "It's part of my kid's Halloween costume, so it should flex without snapping". Opus then called `setup_record`, and the title became "Kid's Halloween arrow headband that flexes without sna…" with the headline "Headband alone in PETG, flat, solid-wall band, no supports". The rule behind this is in the `setup_record` description (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`): the agent may record only a purpose the person stated, and every call must include one. A chat where nobody states a purpose never gets a title or a headline. Kenneth's 2026-10-21 chat, the source of the original screenshot, is such a chat.

**A2. The opening message reads out of place under the card.** It is the first thing in the chat, and nothing above it says a file was opened. The file-load note is drawn as nothing whenever the agent is set up: `bubble()` in `AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx`.

The card always shows the current setup, but the message keeps describing the moment the file opened. After the purpose turn, the card read "Kid's Halloween arrow headband… · Headband alone in PETG · ~1h 05m · 23 g". Directly under it, the opening message still discussed the test square, the two materials and the temperature conflict, and asked "Which printer will you print this on?" All of those had been settled (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`). The find_my_hollow opening in case (b) has the same mismatch (`sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

**A3 (minor). The card cuts off the title.** The purpose may be up to 60 characters, but the card shows a single line, so this title ended in "sna…".

## Case (b): a model imported into an existing project

**B1. The card keeps the previous print's purpose and headline.** I stated the purpose "Halloween headband costume for my kid", and Sonnet recorded it with the headline "P1S PLA, sturdier walls for the clip, arrow and tool on separate plates". I then imported `Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl`, which is unrelated to the headband. Both stayed the same.

Sonnet wrote that its "earlier plan… needs another look now that this sheet is here", but it didn't call `setup_record` (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). The purpose and plan belong to the chat, and nothing resets them when a model is imported.

**B2. The app knows the plan is out of date, but the card doesn't show it.** The saved chat's plan has `validity: "needs_reassessment"` and `invalidatedBy: "Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl"`, yet the card still said "Confirmed". The flag reaches only the model (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:92`). `card_context` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` sends the card only the purpose and the headline.

**B3. Imports get a row in the chat; the file that opened the project gets none.** Each File › Import shows a change row, "Import Object: <file> · you · <time>", above the agent's reply. The file that created the project gets nothing, so its message has no visible trigger (see A2).

## Side issue: a slice stuck at 80% blocked plate layout

This happened in the Sonnet run and not in the Opus run, where the slice finished in about 45 seconds. Right after the first import, a slice that the agent hadn't started sat at 80% for about two minutes.

- Sonnet's three `plate_layout` calls failed with `busy`, "OrcaSlicer does not add a plate while it slices".
- Its `activity_cancel` call failed with `not_found`, "Nothing the tools started has the handle 133". The agent cannot cancel a slice it did not start.
- File › Import was greyed out until I cancelled the slice with the ✕ beside "Slicing…".

I have not checked whether that slice was stuck or only slow, or what started it.

## Note on picking the model

A new project's chat always starts on the provider's default model, Opus 5.5 for Anthropic. The `jusprin_agent.model` setting in the config file doesn't change that default (`AgentHost::default_chat_model` reads the provider profile). The opening message about a newly opened file therefore can't run on any other model.

content.text:
No, it isn't the best experience. All three problems are design gaps, not chance mistakes by the model, and they come from three causes. The causes below are what I found in the code and the saved chats. Whether each is good UX is my judgment.

**1. The title and headline wait for a purpose the person rarely states.**
- **Cause:** The card's title can come from only one place: a purpose the person said in words, recorded by the agent with `setup_record`. That tool also refuses to record a headline without a purpose. A chat that starts by opening a file never gets one, because the person answers the agent's questions ("Bambu Lab A1") rather than saying what the print is for. So the card falls back to the process preset name and shows no plan, even after the agent has switched printers or changed settings. Your 2026-10-21 chat stayed that way for three days.
- **Why it's poor UX:** The biggest text on the card is a preset name the presets line beneath it already gives. Meanwhile the app already knows what is being printed: the file name and the 3MF's own title ("Arrow Headband"). Requiring the person's own words to record a plan also hides plans the agent has actually carried out.
- **Better:** Before there's a purpose, title the card from the file. Let the agent record a headline once it has acted, with or without a purpose.

**2. Nothing updates the card when what's on the plate changes.**
- **Cause:** The purpose and plan belong to the chat, not to what's on the plate, so an import leaves both in place. The app does notice the change: it marks the plan as needing reassessment and names the import as the reason. But that mark goes only to the model, and the card still says "Confirmed". The model can't fix the record either: the file-loaded skill tells it to "change nothing the person has not asked for", and it may only record a purpose the person stated.
- **Why it's poor UX:** The card states something false, and confidently. Showing nothing would be better than that.
- **Better:** When the plan is marked for reassessment, the card should say so ("Plan needs review · Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl added") instead of "Confirmed". The agent should ask whether the new model belongs to the same print, then record the answer.

**3. The chat never shows the event that started it.**
- **Cause:** When the agent is set up, the note recording the opened file draws nothing. Each import gets a change row, but the open that created the project gets none. My guess is that the project's change history only starts after it is created; I haven't checked that. So the chat opens with the agent talking unprompted.
- **Cause, continued:** The card pinned above always shows the setup as it is now, while the message below it describes the moment the file opened. Once anything changes, the two disagree.
- **Cause, continued:** The opening message also repeats what the card shows (the printer switch, the presets). The skill asks for "a few sentences", but Opus wrote four bullet points ending in a question.
- **Why it's poor UX:** The person has no anchor for what started the conversation, and the top of the chat contradicts the card above it.
- **Better:**
  - Add an "Opened petg-pla+support+interface.3mf · 05:31" row in the same style as the import rows, so the message has a visible trigger.
  - Keep the opening message to what the card can't show: the problem and the one question.

The slice stuck at 80% is a separate question. All I know is that the agent can't cancel a slice it didn't start; I haven't diagnosed why the slice stalled.
Create a task to brainstorm on what the optimal user experience should be. choose Fable as the model or leave the option open for me to choose from.
